newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian markets take dive after Wall Street's plunge.
newsitem.headline: Asian markets take dive after Wall Street's plunge.

text.p: Markets across Asia did a nosedive on Thursday after Wall Street's overnight plunge, with Tokyo falling more than 100 points in early trade and Hong Kong dropping sharply.
On Wednesday, the Dow lost 71 points, or 1.09 percent, to about 6,403 after falling nearly 130 points earlier.
The result was a free fall for nearly every Asian bourse. Only Jakarta and Taiwan moved into positive territory during the morning.
Tokyo stocks remained weak in afternoon trade, unable to shrug off losses after the hefty fall on Wall Street, brokers said.
At 0455 GMT, the Nikkei 225 was down 206.43 points or 1.00 percent at 20,361.95.
"Domestic fundamentals have not changed much and the market wants to see whether Wall Street recovers from the sharp fall on Wednesday," a "Big Four" broker said.
Hong Kong stocks ended the morning lower as nervous investors locked in profits following sharp drops on overseas markets, brokers said.
"This (fall) is a reaction to the S&P and the Dow," said Philip Pang, managing director of Amsteel Securities.
The Hang Seng Index ended the morning session down 143.31 points at 13,046.29, although significantly higher than the morning's low of 12,960.81.
A technical glitch caused chaos at the open, when the index was erroneously shown to have dropped more than 500 points.
Philippine shares were sharply lower in early moderate trade. The composite index shed 31.47 points, or 1.0 pct, to 3129.29 in the first 10 minutes of trading.
"It's the Dow Jones again," said Joey Roxas, president of Eagle Equities.
Australian shares remained lower to the midsession break as local traders watched the slump in U.S markets. At midday, the All Ordinaries index was 17.4 points down at 2,341.9.
New Zealand's NZSE-40 Capital Index eased 13.51 points to 2,364.02. The Singapore benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index eased 10.62 points to 2,181.83 at 0215 GMT.

Malaysian stocks opened lower in reaction to Wall Street's fall and on lingering jitters following Wednesday's bout of negative rumours, traders said. At about 0220 GMT, Kuala Lumpur's Composite Index was down 5.0 points to 1,199.39.
Thai stocks fell slightly in thin early trade. The SET index dipped 8.27 points to 877.59 on 263 million baht turnover after the first 29 minutes of trading.

In Korea, stocks were lower at midday as selling spread on profit-taking and bleak prospects for a market rebound, brokers said. The composite index was down 6.76 points to 697.92 by the lunch break, after moving in a range from 697.33 to 706.01.

Indonesian shares defied regional sentiment and rose on increases in heavyweight telecommunications stock Telkom and several secondaries. After 25 minutes of trading, the Jakarta Composite Index rose 1.66 points, or 0.26 percent, to 628.23 points.

Taiwan stocks were weaker in slow mid-morning trade. After 100 minutes of trade, the index had lost 19.00 points, or 0.28 percent, at 6,783.74. By 0400 GMT, however, the market had ventured into positive territory.
